paragraphs: Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud Taanit, chapter 1, halakhah 6, for the mention, but notes that the statement also appears in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, chapter 5, halakhah 2, where the name appears as Rabbi Tanchuma Adra’ah.

notes.text: The Guggenheimer digital text of Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:2 has Tanchuma [Adreiyya], supporting the second occurrence and its name form. The supplied Taanit 1:6 occurrence remains unlocated in the returned research, so that citation remains open.

The parallel previously left open appears in the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 1:1, section 5. Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 1240) gives 1:6. In the passage about Elijah’s vow, Taanit names Rabbi Tanchum Adreiyya. In Berakhot 5:2, the first occurrence reads Tanchuma [Adreiyya], with the place name in brackets, and the later occurrence reads Tanchum Adreiyya. Korban HaEdah on the Taanit passage glosses Adreiyya as a place name.
